features.name: Nothing published until both sign-offs are green
features.label: nothing published until both are green
features.promise: A publish cannot proceed until both the code review (screens 11 and 12) and the outcome sign-off (screen 13) have passed, and the publish carries both.
features.howToVerify: With a change whose code review is approved but whose outcome sign-off is not (and again with the reverse), open the publish step on screen 07 and confirm the destination choices cannot be committed; approve the second one and confirm the same publish then proceeds and shows both sign-offs attached.
features.notes: Flow map edge label 43:91 and the "Choose where it goes" caption 43:40 "Both sign-offs attached".
features.evidence: The publish dialog carries a SIGN-OFFS section with both rows ("Code review - Is it safe?" and "Outcome sign-off - Does it do the job?", both "Not signed off yet") and both gate destinations were refused. distributionGate() requires code and outcome to be verdict 'approved' AND to cover the packet (covers() via sameCommit), refusing at 'no-brief', 'no-packet', 'stale-packet', 'changes-requested', 'awaiting-code', 'awaiting-outcome' and 'same-signer' before it will answer 'open'. The confirm button read "Pick a destination" and was disabled, and the footer said "Nothing is ticked, so nothing will be published." The positive half (approve both, then the same publish proceeds) could not be exercised: creating a packet needs a hand-over to GitHub and the barn-settings Secret holds no token, so no packet exists to sign against. Judged on the enforcement, which is what the rule is about, and which holds.

features.name: The brief sits on the main path before the build
features.label: Agree the brief — The need, the open questions, the criteria · Screen 10
features.promise: Agreeing the brief is a required stage between describing what you want (screen 02) and building it (screen 03), unlike checking the diff yourself (screen 04), which is explicitly optional.
features.howToVerify: Create a new extension from screen 02 and confirm the route passes through the brief on screen 10 before the workspace on screen 03; confirm by contrast that screen 04 can be skipped.
features.notes: Flow map: green connectors 43:50 and 43:53 put 43:11 between 43:8 and 43:16 on the main path, while 43:21 marks screen 04 "Optional". Rationale row 44:41: "It is only cheap to catch before the code exists".
features.evidence: The create route passes through the brief. new-extension.vue's create() calls ensureExtension() and then pushes BRIEF_ROUTE with the prompt, outcome and placement in the query (line 229) - there is no path from screen 02 to the workspace that skips it. brief.vue's agree() then pushes EDITOR_ROUTE with query brief=1, which the workspace picks up and sends to the assistant as the session's first instruction (line 1181). So 02 -> 10 -> 03, which is the flow map's green run. By contrast screen 04 is only reachable from a "Review N changes" affordance and nothing routes through it. Both screens render in the installed bundle (/barn/extensions/new and /barn/extensions/base/brief). Two caveats stated rather than buried: the brief screen carries a ghost "Skip the brief" button that pushes EDITOR_ROUTE directly (brief.vue:1192), so the stage is on the path but not unskippable - though distributionGate() then refuses at 'no-brief', so skipping only defers it to the gate; and the import path (onImported) lands on the studio home rather than the brief, which is a different entry from the flow map's "describe what you want". I did not create an extension to watch the route run, because that provisions another pod into the shared namespace.

features.name: No capability of the current build is lost
features.label: Keeps everything the current build does: CLI, files, GitHub import, publish, settings.
features.promise: The redesign is additive: the CLI, the files view, GitHub import, publish and settings all remain available, and the raw terminal output in particular is still reachable one click away and still the source of truth.
features.howToVerify: Confirm each of the five capabilities is still reachable in the running Studio, and that the raw assistant output is reachable in one click from the activity stream on screen 03.
features.notes: Cover point one (29:13); rationale row 27:16 "Raw output is still there, one click away, and still the source of truth".
features.defect: The "Show raw output" strip on screen 03 - the control that exists to make good on "the raw terminal output is still there, one click away" - is broken in the installed bundle. One click opens it and it renders "the dev server's log could not be read: HTTP 406" with "The last 0 of them." The cause is one header on a function added this wave: devServerLog (extensions.ts:4369) fetches the pod log with `{ headers: { Accept: 'text/plain' } }`, and the apiserver behind Rancher's proxy refuses that - "only the following media types are accepted: application/json, application/yaml, application/vnd.kube...". I proved it from the page: the same URL returns 406 with Accept: text/plain and 200 with the log body with no Accept header or with */*. Dropping the header is the fix. Scope, so this is not over-read: no capability of the current build was lost - claude's own raw stream is still one click away on the Terminal tab and works, and it is the dev server's log, not the assistant's, that this strip serves. But the control the redesign put on screen 03 for this clause errors on its first click, and it regressed in the same wave that changed the exec and fetch layer.
features.evidence: Four of the five named capabilities are intact and were driven, not just found. CLI: the workspace's Terminal tab attached a live xterm to the pod's tmux session over the exec subresource - I typed `echo barn-w4-cli-check`, saw it echo, and saw claude's own footer ("bypass permissions on (shift+tab to cycle)"). Files: /barn/extensions/base/files renders the tree, ten history entries and an editable pane. GitHub import: the Import dialog does connection as step one, and with no token stored step two degrades correctly to "name the repository below or paste its URL - a public one clones with no token at all", with step three offering branch and name and no link out to settings. Settings: /barn/settings renders connection, permissions, access and data with live values. Publish: the dialog reads the version and changeset out of the pod and runs the pre-flight checks ("Scanned 4 files for tokens, keys and kubeconfigs"); I did not publish. The strict write path through the new exec layer also works from the UI - screen 13's accept-drift wrote BRIEF.md into the pod and I saw the file change. probe-errors.mjs reports ALL CLEAN across all ten screens. What is broken is the raw-output surface this rule names, see the defect.

features.name: A requested change arrives as an assistant instruction
features.label: Goes straight back to the workspace with the comment already loaded into the assistant — the reviewer never writes the fix themselves
features.promise: A reviewer's comment, from either the code review or the outcome sign-off, is carried into the author's workspace already loaded into the assistant as the instruction to work from, and the reviewer is never asked to write the fix.
features.howToVerify: Comment on a hunk on screen 12 and use "Send to the assistant", then open the author's workspace on screen 03 and confirm the reviewer's exact wording is present as a pending assistant instruction that the author must still approve.
features.notes: Flow map "Changes requested" (43:44/43:46) is fed by amber arrows from both "Code review" (43:82) and "Outcome sign-off" (43:85); rationale row 44:32 adds "the author still approves it".
features.evidence: Verified end to end this wave. Commented on hunk 26 of product.ts on screen 12 with "w4-cross probe: rename this variable to nodeConditionTrend (verifier w4-cross-screen)" and pressed Send to the assistant. The barn-review-base ConfigMap recorded the comment with sentAt 2026-08-23T19:46:05.786Z and sentHow "sent", and `tmux capture-pane -t mc-editor` in the pod shows it arrived verbatim, wrapped as a reviewer instruction: "A reviewer looked at this change and asked for something. It is about pages/Home.vue around line 10. Their words: w4-cross probe: rename this variable to nodeConditionTrend (verifier w4-cross-screen). Make that change in the working tree and explain what you did." The reviewer wrote no code, and the author still approves: the assistant answered "Not logged in - Please run /login" and changed nothing. Screen 12 also offers rc-comment-record-N (record without sending) beside rc-comment-send-N, so sending is a deliberate second act.

features.name: One diff against the last published version
features.label: collapsed into one diff against the last published version
features.promise: The reviewer is shown a single diff of the change against the last published version, not the sequence of intermediate edits that produced it.
features.howToVerify: Make an edit and then undo or supersede it before pushing, then open the change on screen 12 and confirm the diff shows only the net difference from the last published version and no intermediate state.
features.notes: Guardrail note 43:93 on the flow map.
features.evidence: Every diff on the review surfaces is one `git diff <baseline>` (BASELINE_SH in extensions.ts resolves refs/barn/published/oci, then refs/barn/published/local, then HEAD), so intermediate commits collapse by construction. Demonstrated on base: verify-w2-review.txt was added and then removed across the intermediate commits 2abd586..24b3922, and it appears nowhere in the whole-change reading (4 files: HARNESS.md, product.ts, verify-w4-workspace.txt, w4-review.generated.ts) - only the net state is shown. Measuring from 2abd586 instead (?from=2abd586) brings it back as "deleted -1", which is the same collapse taken from a different point. Screen 04 says the same thing in words: "Nothing here has reached the repository yet. Everything here is in the pod's working tree." One caveat: screen 12 does not read baselineRef(), so its scope notice says "measured from the last published version" even on base, where nothing has ever been published and the baseline is really HEAD. Screen 04 does read baselineRef and says which point it used.

features.name: Connection state and permission mode are one state shown in two places
features.label: Connection state is a persistent strip in the panel: a dot, the account, and the permission mode as a real control.
features.promise: The account, connection state and assistant permission mode shown on the workspace strip (screen 03) and on the settings page (screen 09) are the same state, and settings is the one place all of it lives.
features.howToVerify: Change the permission mode on screen 09 and confirm the workspace strip on screen 03 reflects it without a reload, and vice versa; confirm no other modal edits the GitHub token.
features.notes: Rationale rows 27:25 ("Screens 03, 09") and 27:34; caption 23:918 "connection, permissions, access and data in one place", replacing the bare token modal (23:919).
features.defect: Unchanged from the previous wave. (1) The permission mode is not a control on either screen, so it cannot be changed in one place and seen in the other, and the design's "the permission mode as a real control" on screen 03 does not exist. The settings page is honest about why, which is right, but honesty is not the promise. (2) components/EditorSettingsModal.vue still stores and removes the GitHub token and is opened from screens 02, 03 and 12; it shares studio-settings.ts with the settings page so the two cannot disagree, and it deliberately offers only the credential, but screen 09's caption has it replacing the token modal outright.
features.evidence: Re-checked both halves against the installed bundle; neither has changed. The settings page's permission card is explicit that there is nothing to change: "Not settable, and not per user. The pod starts claude with --dangerously-skip-permissions (pod/claude-session.sh), so this is the level in force for everybody... a level chosen here would be undone within seconds". The workspace strip shows barn-permission-chip reading "Edits apply without asking", which is a statement, not the control the design draws. And a second surface still edits the GitHub token: I clicked the "No GitHub token" chip on screen 12 and EditorSettingsModal opened with a single password field placeholder ghp_..., titled "Connect GitHub", with an "All Studio settings" link back to screen 09. It is reachable from screens 02, 03 and 12.

features.name: Verification walks the criteria written in the brief
features.label: Acceptance criteria written in the brief become a checklist walked against the running build, with captured evidence and a second, separate sign-off.
features.promise: The acceptance criteria are authored once on screen 10 and are the same items walked, against the running build and with evidence captured, on screen 13.
features.howToVerify: Write a distinctive acceptance criterion in the brief on screen 10, take the change through to verification, and confirm screen 13 lists that exact criterion as a checklist item, exercised against the running build, with the captured evidence attached.
features.notes: Rationale row 44:59 ("Screens 07 and 13"); caption 45:1206 "the criteria walked against the running build"; flow map 43:37.
features.evidence: Read base's BRIEF.md in the pod: "## How we will know it worked" lists four items, two ticked. /barn/extensions/base/verification lists those same four items in the same order, as the checklist, with the two ticked ones showing "evidence captured" and the other two "not measured" - nothing is re-entered on screen 13 and nothing is invented. Screen 12 shows the same four under "DOES IT DO THE JOB? 4 criteria", so one authored list feeds both. Screen 13 also frames it correctly ("You are checking whether this does the job, not whether the code is any good") and each criterion has Yes / No / Can't tell plus "Show me", walked against the live preview pane on the right, and the note says recording the result ticks the boxes back into BRIEF.md.

features.name: Built from components the dashboard already has
features.label: Everything below is achievable with components that already exist in the Rancher dashboard — SortableTable, LabeledInput, Banner, Card, Tabbed, AsyncButton — so none of this asks the team to invent new UI primitives.
features.promise: Every screen is realisable with existing Rancher dashboard primitives, and the Studio home list in particular uses the same SortableTable pattern as the Clusters page rather than a bespoke table.
features.howToVerify: Inspect the rendered markup of the Studio screens and confirm tables, inputs, banners, cards, tabs and async buttons are the dashboard's own components rather than reimplementations, and that screen 01 reads like the Clusters page table.
features.notes: Header note 27:5 of the rationale frame; rationale row 27:88 names the Clusters page pattern for screen 01.
features.defect: The Studio is built almost entirely on its own primitives, so Banner, Card, Tabbed and SortableTable are all reimplementations, and screen 01 in particular is a hand-rolled div table with its own sort buttons rather than the SortableTable pattern the rationale names (27:5, 27:91). The reimplementations are competent and the sort affordances work; the rule is about not needing new primitives, and the product needed fifteen.
features.evidence: Re-checked, unchanged. `grep -rn "from '@shell|from '@components|from '@rancher"` over pkg/barn finds Rancher components in only five files, none of which is one of the ten screens: ExtensionFiles, ExtensionSelect, NewExtensionModal, PublishStatus and PublishSplit. Every screen is drawn with components/ui's own SBadge, SBanner, SButton, SCard, SChip, SEmpty, SField, SIcon, SLabel, SMenu, SModal, SPanel, SRow, STabs, SToolbar. SortableTable appears nowhere in the package. I dumped screen 01's rendered markup and it is a div grid - `<div class="studio-home__table"><div class="studio-home__head"><button class="studio-home__th" aria-sort="none">` - not a table element and not the Clusters page's SortableTable.

features.name: A guaranteed way back from any build failure
features.label: When it breaks — plain-language cause, one-click fix, guaranteed way back
features.promise: Every build is snapshotted so that a failure always has a state to roll back to, which means the snapshot has to be taken in the workspace before the change that breaks it.
features.howToVerify: Cause a build to fail from a known-good state and confirm screen 08 offers a snapshot of that state to roll back to, and that rolling back returns the workspace to it.
features.notes: Caption 23:915 and rationale row 27:97 "a snapshot to roll back to"; the snapshot is created on screen 03 and consumed on screen 08.
features.evidence: The guarantee now holds and the point is durable. The sessionStorage record is gone: publishExtension writes refs/barn/working-build via recordBaseline at the moment a build has installed (extensions.ts:2197, :4082), lastWorkingBuild reads it back out of the pod, and readWorkingBuild is what BuildFailure.findWayBack reaches for first. I proved the write mechanism actually works in the pod rather than trusting it: ran recordBaseline's exact shell by hand in barn-base-extension against a scratch ref (GIT_INDEX_FILE, read-tree, add -A, write-tree, commit-tree -p HEAD, update-ref) - it produced 244643c, `git log -1 --format='%H%x1f%s%x1f%cr'` returned exactly what lastWorkingBuild parses, and neither HEAD nor the index moved. I deleted the ref and the root-owned .git/refs/barn it left behind. findWayBack has four tiers and always lands on one, and it says which it landed on rather than implying the best case: on base, which has never been published, screen 08 offered an enabled "Roll back to the snapshot 'autosave 1932 on Aug 23'" (taken 2 minutes earlier by EditorMasthead.autoSnapshot, which fingerprints the working diff and snapshots when it moves) with the note "no build of this extension has succeeded here yet, so this is the nearest point that exists rather than a build that is known to have worked". So the design's "snapshot taken before the change that breaks it" exists in practice via the autosave, and the durable ref is the better point when a build has actually succeeded. The exec fix is what makes this real: createSnapshot now verifies its tag afterwards instead of sending git tag to /dev/null, and the pod has four live barn-snap tags. I did not click Roll back - it would have destroyed four other verifiers' uncommitted work in the shared base pod - so "rolling back returns the workspace to it" is read off the code (restoreSnapshot, and the panel refusing when the safety snapshot cannot be taken) rather than observed.

features.name: Iteration before the gate asks nobody
features.label: Iteration is completely ungated: dev preview and developer load ask nobody.
features.promise: Creating, building, previewing, breaking, rebuilding and developer-loading an extension never require anyone's approval, so no review or sign-off control may block any of them.
features.howToVerify: Make several edits in the workspace (screen 03), let a build fail and recover it (screen 08), and developer-load the result, confirming that no approval dialog, pending-review banner or disabled control appears at any point before screen 07.
features.notes: Rationale row 65:1083; flow map caption 43:18 "Readable activity, live preview, and no gates at all" and 43:24 "Everything before it is yours alone".
features.evidence: Drove /barn/editor, /barn/extensions/base/files, /barn/extensions/base/review, /barn/extensions/base/build-failed and /barn/extensions/base/verification: no approval dialog, no pending-review banner and no disabled control on any of them. Typed into the pod terminal (`echo barn-w4-cli-check` echoed back) with nobody asked. The publish dialog labels the local load and the GitHub source push "No sign-off" and states "Loading this into a Rancher to try it, or handing it over on GitHub to ask for a review, needs nobody." Settings goes further: settings-signoff-enforcement says the sign-off matrix records intent only, and "a developer load reaches only this Rancher and is ungated" is fixed in code, with the publish dialog naming any stored value it is not obeying (I saw it do exactly that: "Settings put an outcome sign-off at 'Notified'. The gate takes both regardless").

features.name: The OCI publish gate
features.label: Push to an OCI repository — The one hard gate. Everything before it is yours alone · Screen 07
features.promise: There is exactly one hard gate in the whole product and it is the push to an OCI repository, the point at which the extension first becomes installable by other people.
features.howToVerify: From a freshly created extension, walk stages 01, 02, 10, 03 and 04 without ever being asked for an approval, then start a publish to an OCI repository on screen 07 and confirm that this is the first and only step that will not complete on the author's say-so alone.
features.notes: Flow map 43:22/43:24 and the guardrail note 43:93; rationale row 65:1083 states it as "The gate is the push to an OCI repository, where the extension first becomes installable by other people".
features.evidence: Opened the publish dialog on base (installed bundle 0.5.22) without publishing. Five destinations, and exactly two carry a "The gate" tag - "Push to an OCI repository" and "Put the reviewed packet on the repository", which the dialog names as the same distribution boundary reached by the two routes this Studio has. "Load into this Rancher" and "Push the source to GitHub" both read "No sign-off", and the catalog row is "Both + extensions team" and explicitly not tickable. Both gate rows were refused with `barn-publish-gate-oci` / `-repository` reading "This change has never been handed over, so nobody has been asked to review it." distributionGate() in review.ts is the single enforcement point and it is only consulted by the two gate rows.

features.name: The hand-off to review is a PR, and the PR is the record
features.label: hand-off · the PR is the record
features.promise: Crossing the gate hands the work from the author's lane to the reviewers' lane by producing a PR, and that PR is the durable record of the hand-off.
features.howToVerify: Push a change to an OCI repository and confirm the resulting queue entry on screen 11 is backed by a PR, and that the PR is reachable from the review surface as the record of the change.
features.notes: Flow map connector label 43:90 on the green connector running from "Push to an OCI repository" (43:22) into "Code review" (43:28).
features.defect: packetPullRequest() has landed but nothing calls it, so the fix is dead code and screen 12 is unchanged. review-change.vue:1644 checkPullRequest() still searches GitHub for an open PR whose head is listBranches().current; a packet's branch is made with `git branch -f` and never checked out, so that branch is never the packet's. The visible consequence on base (never handed over) is a chip saying "No GitHub token" where packetPullRequest() would say "This has never been handed over, so there is no pull request to be its record yet" - the accurate answer, and one that needs no token. The change is to import packetPullRequest from review.ts and drive prState/pr from its six states instead of the four checkPullRequest computes. Secondary and unchanged: with no token in the barn-settings Secret and no repository remembered, the hand-over refuses before it reaches GitHub, so no queue entry backed by a real PR can be produced in this environment.
features.evidence: review.ts:945 packetPullRequest() now exists and does the right thing: it answers from the packet record first (state 'recorded'), only asks GitHub about packet.branch, and has a 'no-packet' state whose sentence is "This has never been handed over, so there is no pull request to be its record yet." But `grep -rn packetPullRequest pkg/barn` finds no caller outside its own definition. Screen 12 still runs the old checkPullRequest() at review-change.vue:1644, which reads `this.branch = branches?.current` and calls findOpenPullRequest(extension, repo, this.branch). Driving /barn/review/base/working in the installed bundle, the chip read "No GitHub token" with the title "No GitHub token is configured, so nothing can be asked. Opens the editor settings." - the token state, not the hand-over state, and clicking it opened EditorSettingsModal rather than a PR.

features.name: Preview and published are separated by an explicit line
features.label: The same live preview, plus an explicit boundary: preview is yours alone, snapshotted per build, and publishing is a separate deliberate act.
features.promise: Work in the live preview affects only the author and is snapshotted per build; nothing reaches anyone else until the separate, deliberate publish on screen 07.
features.howToVerify: Make a visible change in the workspace preview on screen 03, then confirm from another session or another user that the installed extension is unchanged until a publish is performed on screen 07.
features.notes: Rationale row 27:52 ("Screens 03, 07"); the cover's reading note 29:41 calls it "an explicit line between preview and published".
features.evidence: base has four changed files in its pod and a live preview rendering in the workspace's right pane, and it is not installed anywhere: the only UIPlugins in the cluster are barn 0.5.22 and nodehealth 0.1.0, and the home row's "Remove the local install" is disabled with "not installed". So nothing about working in the preview has published anything. The line is drawn in words too, in three places: the workspace says "2 changes - Only you can see them. Nothing is asked of you until you publish", screen 04 says "Nothing here has reached the repository yet. Everything here is in the pod's working tree", and the publish dialog says every destination is a separate choice with none ticked. Snapshotted per build is the autosave in EditorMasthead (four barn-snap tags in the pod, the newest 2 minutes old when I looked).

features.name: Prompt provenance and the brief survive from authoring into review
features.label: Every hunk carries the prompt that produced it, and the whole change carries its brief.
features.promise: The prompt that caused each hunk is captured during authoring on screen 03 and is still attached, per hunk, when the change is reviewed on screen 12, and the brief from screen 10 travels with the change as a whole.
features.howToVerify: Author a change with two distinguishable prompts in the workspace, push it, then on screen 12 confirm each hunk shows the prompt that produced it and that the change header shows the brief written on screen 10.
features.notes: Rationale row 44:5; caption 45:1204 "prompt provenance per hunk".
features.evidence: Both halves of the path are wired and the capture half was verified live this wave. The brief travels: screen 12's header on base renders WHAT THIS IS FOR / WHO HAS IT / WHAT CHANGES FOR THEM / WHAT WE ARE DELIBERATELY NOT DOING read out of the extension's own BRIEF.md, with a line saying which section each came from. The capture: I sent a comment from screen 12 to the assistant and then read the pod's own turn log (`node /seed/barn-provenance.mjs turns 5`), which had recorded it as turn tmt67wfq06176y with the full prompt, screen "review-comment", principal local://user-btc48 and who "Default Admin" - and had separately recorded the line I typed straight into the terminal with an empty screen, which is the honest distinction. The review half renders per hunk: each hunk carried its own strip, here in the unrecorded state ("4 lines changed in the pod, no prompt recorded") with a summary "No prompt recorded for any of this change's 8 lines". A hunk carrying a real prompt could not be produced in this environment: claude has no credentials in any of the three pods ("Not logged in - Please run /login"), so no turn ends in a commit, `commit` is "" on every recorded turn, and no commit anywhere carries a Barn-Turn trailer for provenanceFor() to blame a line back to.

features.name: Live is reversible from the extension list
features.label: Reversible from the extension list
features.promise: Publishing is not a one-way door: a live extension can be taken back from the Studio home list on screen 01.
features.howToVerify: Publish an extension, return to /dashboard/barn/extensions, and confirm the row for the live extension offers a way to reverse the publish.
features.notes: Flow map terminal state "Live" (43:41) and its caption 43:43; the reversal control lives on screen 01, not on screen 07.
features.evidence: The overflow menu on each row of /barn/extensions carries "Remove the local install". On nodehealth, which is installed (the row reads "catalog - v0.1.0" and a UIPlugin nodehealth 0.1.0 exists in the cluster), the item read "Remove the local install v0.1.0" and was enabled. On base and demo, neither of which is installed, the same item read "Remove the local install not installed" and was disabled, so it tracks the real UIPlugin rather than being decorative. The publish dialog states the same contract from the other end: "Reversible: 'Remove local install' takes it back off." I did not click it - uninstalling nodehealth would have pulled it out from under the other verifiers.

features.name: Every recovery route returns to the same workspace
features.label: amber is recovery — and every recovery route leads back into the same workspace rather than out of the product
features.promise: Both failure routes drawn on the map, a broken build and a rejected review, end back in the author's workspace rather than in a separate remediation surface or outside the product.
features.howToVerify: Trigger a build failure and apply its fix, confirming the user lands back in the same workspace; separately, request changes as a reviewer and confirm the author is returned to that same workspace rather than to a new screen.
features.notes: Flow map legend 43:4; the amber arrows 43:62/43:65 leave and re-enter the same "Build it and watch it" box (43:16), and "Changes requested" (43:44) routes back to it.
features.evidence: Both amber routes end in the same workspace. Build failure: seeded barn.publish.failure and loaded /barn/extensions/base/build-failed - the card carries barn-to-workspace "Back to the workspace" and the apply-fix and roll-back actions all sit on that one panel rather than routing anywhere new. Rejected review: review-change.vue's requestChanges() (line ~1624) and its send-comment handler (line ~1501) both `$router.push({ name: EDITOR_ROUTE, params: { extension }, query: { tab: 'terminal' } })`, and I saw the send do it - the page left .rc__body immediately after "Send to the assistant" landed. Screen 13's hand-back does the same, and its own panel carries "Back to the workspace". No separate remediation surface exists anywhere in pages/.

features.name: The review packet accumulates in the background and is assembled at the push
features.label: the review packet accumulates quietly in the background. It is only assembled and handed to a reviewer at the push to a repository
features.promise: Everything a reviewer will need is captured continuously while the author works, but it is only assembled into a review packet and handed over at the moment of the push.
features.howToVerify: Work in the workspace for several build cycles without publishing and confirm nothing appears in the review queue (screen 11), then push once and confirm a complete packet, including material captured across all of those earlier cycles, appears in a single queue entry.
features.notes: Guardrail note 43:93 on the flow map.
features.defect: handedOverExtensions() has landed but nothing calls it. review-queue.vue:368 load() still enumerates every extension from listExtensions() and enriches each, so an author's dirty working tree is a row in somebody else's queue and counts toward "Waiting on you". The row explains itself in words and carries a queue-not-handed chip, which is honest, but a row that explains why it should not be there is still a row. The change is to filter `summaries` through handedOverExtensions(names) before mapping them into this.rows.
features.evidence: review.ts:1051 handedOverExtensions() now exists and answers exactly the queue's question (one ConfigMap read per extension, in parallel, an extension with no packets is not handed over). `grep -rn handedOverExtensions pkg/barn` finds no caller outside its own definition. review-queue.vue's load() (line 368) still does `const summaries = await listExtensions()` and then `enrich()` on every one of them. Driving /barn/review in the installed bundle: base - whose barn-review-base ConfigMap has `"packets": {}` and which has never been handed over - is a row in the queue, the header reads "Waiting on you 1", and the row itself says "Never handed over, so nobody has been asked to review it. It is still the author's own working tree." So "work for several build cycles without publishing and confirm nothing appears in the review queue" still does not hold.

features.name: The build is compared back to its own brief at sign-off
features.label: The build is compared back to its own brief, and anything outside it is flagged during sign-off — accept it into the brief, or take it out.
features.promise: At outcome sign-off the built change is diffed against the brief that started it, and anything not in the brief is surfaced with two resolutions: accept it into the brief, or remove it.
features.howToVerify: Have the assistant make a change beyond what the brief asked for, take it to screen 13, and confirm the extra work is flagged as outside the brief and offers both accepting it into the brief and taking it out.
features.notes: Rationale row 44:68; requires the screen 10 brief to still be attached to the change at screen 13.
features.defect: The detection is still the half that does not hold. scopeDrift() is a word match: it takes up to six terms out of the brief's "What we are deliberately not doing" section and looks for them in the change's added lines. So work that is outside the brief but does not happen to reuse one of those words is not flagged at all, and an extension whose brief has no non-goals section gets "there is nothing to measure the change against" rather than a comparison. The design's clause is "the build is compared back to its own brief, and anything outside it is flagged", which a term match over one section cannot deliver. Second, smaller: accepting one term accepts the whole sentence it was found in. base's non-goals were "No alerting, and no history beyond 24 hours. Both belong in monitoring." - accepting "alerting" moved that entire sentence out, leaving the section as "_not stated_", so the untouched non-goal about 24-hour history was silently accepted too and every later scope check on that extension answers "nothing to measure against".
features.evidence: Half of this closed this wave and half did not, so it is worth being precise. The two resolutions now exist and both work. I added a line containing "alerting" to base's working tree (verify-w4-cross.txt) - a word base's brief lists under what it is deliberately not doing - and screen 13's Scope card moved from "Nothing this change adds mentions monitoring/alerting/history/... " to a drift row naming the term and the file, with verify-accept-drift-alerting ("That is fine - add it to the brief") and verify-remove-drift-alerting ("Remove it") beside it. Clicking accept rewrote BRIEF.md for real - the non-goals line moved into "What changes for them" stamped "(accepted during verification on 2026-08-23 by admin)" - and the warning went. removeDrift is wired to askAssistant with the term, the files and an instruction not to touch BRIEF.md; I did not fire it into the shared pod. I restored BRIEF.md from my backup and removed the probe file afterwards.

features.name: Re-review is incremental across visits
features.label: A "since your last look" filter, and a banner on the queue row saying how many changes landed since you approved.
features.promise: Per-reviewer state persists between visits, so a reviewer returning after the author has pushed again sees how many changes landed since they approved and can filter the diff to just those.
features.howToVerify: Approve a change as a reviewer, push further changes as the author, then return to screen 11 and confirm the queue row banners the number of changes since that approval, and that screen 12 offers a "since your last look" filter restricted to them.
features.notes: Rationale row 44:23, "Screens 11 and 12".
features.evidence: Both halves now work, driven against the installed bundle. changedFilesSince/fileDiffSince (extensions.ts:2505, :2527) take an arbitrary commit, and screen 12 uses them for both the list and the patch. /barn/review/base/working?scope=since&from=2abd586 narrowed to 5 files with an info banner "Showing what has landed since 2abd586, the commit your approval was given against: 5 files. The whole change, measured from the last published version, is 4 files. Approve still commits all of it." The narrowed list is genuinely a different measurement, not a subset: it contains verify-w2-review.txt as "deleted -1", a file absent from the 4-file whole-change reading, and selecting it rendered its deletion patch, so the diff moves with the list. Toggling the chip with no ?from used the recorded look (24b3922) and said so. Refusal is real rather than a silent fallback: ?from=deadbeef...(40 hex, not a commit) put the chip in error tone and rendered rc-scope-refused - "...it could not be measured: deadbeef... is not a commit in base any more, so there is nothing to measure from. The whole change is shown instead, and nothing has been hidden from you." The queue side is wired to it: review-queue.vue's openSince() opens the same route with scope=since and from set to the commit the approval was given against.

features.name: Two sign-offs by two different people
features.label: Splits "is it safe?" from "does it work?" — two questions, two people, neither able to answer the other's.
features.promise: The code review is signed by a developer and the outcome sign-off by the person who asked for the change; they are separate acts by separate roles, not one approval recorded twice.
features.howToVerify: Confirm the code review record (screen 12) and the verification record (screen 13) carry distinct signer identities and distinct timestamps, and that signing one does not mark the other complete.
features.notes: Rationale row 44:59; flow map 43:32 "A developer" and 43:37 "The person who asked"; cover point three 29:21 "a separate outcome sign-off by the person who asked".
features.evidence: The two records are separate objects: review.json's signoffs.code (written by signCodeReview on screen 12) and signoffs.outcome (signOutcome on screen 13), each carrying its own principal, name, at and sha, and neither write touches the other. The publish dialog draws them as two rows with two different questions and a note that "Two people answer two questions". distributionGate() has an explicit 'same-signer' refusal that fires when code.principal === outcome.principal, with the reason "one person answering both is one opinion recorded twice". Confirmed against the live barn-review-base ConfigMap, whose signoffs object is keyed code/outcome.

features.name: See when the last snapshot was taken
features.label: Snapshot saved 12s ago
features.promise: A clock line tells you the workspace autosaves and when the last snapshot happened.
features.howToVerify: Load https://magic-closet-rancher/dashboard/barn/editor, make an edit, wait, and check the 'Snapshot saved Ns ago' text updates.
features.notes: icon/clock (5:119) plus text 9:206.
features.evidence: Both halves of the line are true now. The workspace does autosave: with the editor open I wrote W4-AUTOSAVE-1787516372511 into a file in the pod, and 10 seconds later a new tag barn-snap/1787516405029 "autosave 2020 on Aug 23" existed, whose tree really holds my edit (git show barn-snap/1787516405029:verify-w4-workspace.txt returns exactly that marker). Nobody took it by hand. It is rate limited from the newest snapshot in the pod rather than per tab: the gaps between consecutive autosave tags over an hour were 188, 181, 182, 181, 180, 184, 184 and 180 seconds - never under three minutes - while the two safety snapshots taken by an apply and a roll back sat between them at 47s and 62s, as they should. A second edit ten seconds after an autosave produced no new snapshot for at least 110 seconds; the readout just kept counting up. And the readout is a real clock on the newest snapshot: "Snapshot saved 27h ago" on arrival with one 27-hour-old tag in the pod, then "Snapshot saved 9s / 2m / 3m ago" as they were taken, with the tooltip naming the snapshot it is reporting. Finally, it says so when it fails: with .git/objects and .git/refs root-owned in the pod and the tree moving, the line changed to "Autosave failed - last snapshot 4m ago" and the tooltip to "The tree has changed and it could not be snapshotted, so nothing since \"autosave 2020 on Aug 23\" is kept: the snapshot of base failed in the pod (exit 1): error: insufficient permission for adding an object to repository ...". features.name: Show the raw command output

features.howToVerify: From https://magic-closet-rancher/dashboard/barn/editor click 'Show raw output' and check raw build output expands inline, then click again to collapse.
features.notes: Frame named 'raw output (collapsed)': icon/terminal 32:894, label 32:897, hint 32:899 'the terminal is still here', icon/chevronDown 32:900.
features.defect: devServerLog() in extensions.ts fetches the pod-log subresource with { headers: { Accept: 'text/plain' } }. The Kubernetes apiserver rejects that: 406 NotAcceptable, "only the following media types are accepted: application/json, application/yaml, application/vnd.kubernetes.protobuf". Verified from the page: the same URL with no Accept header, or with Accept: */*, returns 200 text/plain with the log. Dropping the header fixes it. Until then the strip expands onto an error every time. Noted while writing this up: the working tree already carries that fix, but it is not in the installed bundle this wave was judged against.
features.evidence: The strip does now expand in place: clicking [data-testid=barn-open-raw-output] flips aria-expanded false -> true, the label to "Hide raw output", and a panel opens under it with a Re-read button and the note "The pod's own log, with the progress redraws and the terminal control codes taken out." Clicking again collapses it and the panel goes. What never arrives is the log: the body reads "the dev server's log could not be read: HTTP 406" and the footer says "The last 0 of them", on a pod whose log is 600+ lines of webpack output.

features.name: Discard every change

features.notes: Button/Ghost with icon/trash. Destructive; check for a confirmation.
features.defect: The narrowing is coded but never runs, because `baselineRef()` in extensions.ts:2250 cannot execute. Its script is assembled as an array joined with ' ; ', and the second element ends in `do`, so the join inserts a stray semicolon: `for r in refs/barn/published/oci refs/barn/published/local ; do ; git rev-parse ...`. The pod's /bin/sh (dash) answers `Syntax error: ";" unexpected` and exits 2 - I captured that frame off the exec WebSocket on a live page load, and reproduced it by hand in the pod; removing the stray `;` prints KIND=refs/barn/published/local and SHA=24b3922... correctly. `inPackage` returns only stdout, so baselineRef sees '' and returns {kind:'none', sha:'', label:'this extension has no history yet...'}. review.vue's readStates() then short-circuits on `!this.baseline.sha` and returns {}, so `committed` is always empty, `discardable` is always every file, no Keep box is ever disabled, committedNote never renders and discardLabel is always 'Discard all'. Fix: drop the ' ; ' before the `git rev-parse` element (or join that pair with a space). Same call is used by BuildFailure.vue and studio/PreviewPanel.vue, so their baseline sentences are wrong for the same reason.
features.evidence: On base with no published ref (baseline == HEAD) the button reads 'Discard all' and is the honest no-op the wave describes. I then created the other condition: `git update-ref refs/barn/published/local 24b3922` with HEAD two commits ahead, so four of the six listed files (HARNESS.md, product.ts, verify-w4-workspace.txt, w4-review.generated.ts) were committed and unreachable by a discard. The screen did not narrow: every Keep box was enabled with the ordinary 'Untick to revert...' title, [data-testid=review-committed-note] was absent, and the button still read 'Discard all' over 6 files. Reproduced twice.

features.name: Roll back from the changes summary
features.label: Roll back
features.promise: A secondary button in the summary strip rolls the workspace back to the last working build.
features.howToVerify: Click 'Roll back' in the summary strip and confirm the preview returns to the last working build.
features.notes: Same action as the masthead's 19:959.
features.evidence: Drove both outcomes against a file of my own. Refusal first: with .git/objects and .git/refs root-owned in the pod, clicking "Roll back to ..." gave "The roll back did not happen - Nothing has been rolled back. The failed tree could not be snapshotted first, and this panel will not replace a tree it cannot put back: the snapshot of base failed in the pod (exit 1): error: insufficient permission for adding an object to repository database .git/objects ...". Afterwards the file was byte-for-byte unchanged, the snapshot count was still 18, the failure card was still on screen, the badge still read Failed and the button was still offered. Then chowned back to 1000:1000, wrote refs/barn/working-build at a commit holding the tree, and the button relabelled itself "Roll back to the last working build (9.9.9-w4)". Changed my file to W4-ROLLBACK-MODIFIED and clicked: toast "Rolled back to the last working build (9.9.9-w4) - The failed tree was snapshotted first, so nothing is lost.", the file was back to W4-ROLLBACK-BEFORE, a new tag "the failed build before rolling back" existed and git show of my file at that tag returned W4-ROLLBACK-MODIFIED, the failure card was gone and the badge went back to Unsaved. The ref was removed afterwards.
